verdict.root_cause: cartservice is serving every request successfully but each cache round trip to its Redis-style backend takes a near-constant ~300ms, and cartservice handlers do essentially nothing but wait on those calls (handler spans exceed their child cache spans by only 1-3ms). Because AddItem makes two sequential cache calls it costs ~600ms, and the delay propagates unchanged up the call chain: checkoutservice PlaceOrder (~650ms) is almost entirely its GetCart and EmptyCart legs, and frontend POST spans reach ~900ms+ (tr_781267aff6ff). No errors are produced anywhere — cartservice and checkoutservice error ratios are real, populated zeros across the full window (tr_ae82f54828de, tr_2ffacf2eb0c4, tr_314c1e8e5e81) — and cartservice logs show continuous healthy request handling after onset with no dependency named (tr_3156839129b2). This is a latency-only impairment of the cache dependency, not an error, not a crash, and not the two past cart incidents in the corpus where the process was not running at all. The uniformity of the ~300ms across reads and writes, all trace ids, and all endpoints looks like a fixed stall floor rather than load-driven queueing, but no change record exists for cartservice to explain it (tr_024fd3194000).
verdict.reasoning: The trace evidence localises virtually all added latency to named cache operation spans inside cartservice, with cartservice self-time in the single-digit milliseconds, and rules out the caller hop, cartservice's own logic, checkout orchestration, and every other downstream (all sub-20ms) (tr_781267aff6ff). The failure mechanism is therefore waiting on a dependency, which is dependency_latency — the service is not out of a resource it needs (no saturation metric was ever retrieved, but nothing failed for want of capacity), the artifact is running and serving (tr_3156839129b2, tr_ae82f54828de), and no wrong configuration value has been identified: the cartservice change log is empty for the window including cache/connection settings (tr_024fd3194000), so the bad_config path the corpus's cart-redis-misconfig incident suggests is not supported here — and in that past incident cart never came up at all, whereas here it serves traffic throughout. The flat-zero error ratios are corroborated as real zeros with populated denominators, which distinguishes this from the cart-bad-image-tag pattern where zero meant absence of data. Remediation is named for the mechanism: the cache tier must stop inserting the ~300ms stall, which for a fixed-delay stall floor most plausibly means restarting/restoring the cache backend rather than reverting a change that no log records.
open_questions: The cache backend itself was never dispatched to. Its own latency, saturation, connection state, change history and any injected-delay/fault-injection configuration are entirely unestablished — the ~300ms is inferred from the client side only.

No latency percentile, CPU/memory, or connection-pool metrics were ever retrieved for cartservice despite two metric dispatches (tr_ae82f54828de, tr_2ffacf2eb0c4), so a pool-wait or saturation contribution to the ~300ms cannot be excluded and the exact onset inflection at 05:00:30 is unconfirmed by metrics.

The cartservice log result was truncated and omitted 04:50:34-05:02:46, which contains the 05:00:30 onset (tr_3156839129b2); no evidence covers what cartservice logged at the moment of transition, and the absence of lines after 05:03:13 is unexplained.

Change history was checked only for cartservice and productcatalogservice. The cache/Redis component, frontend, checkoutservice, and the sync-edge peers (adservice, recommendationservice, shippingservice) have no change coverage (tr_396164e67781), so an upstream edit elsewhere that introduced the delay remains open.

Because no change record explains the onset, the correct remediation is genuinely uncertain: restart of the cache tier is the best fit for a fixed stall floor, but if the delay comes from an unlogged config or fault-injection setting, config_revert would be the real fix.
Four unmeasured edges were crossed by triage and 8 of 12 affected services were never dispatched to; whether any of them show independent symptoms is unknown.
